items.stem: Why is a logo not the same as a brand?

options.text: A brand is the overall perception and relationship; the logo is one identifier of it
options.rationale: Correct: the brand is the perception; the logo only signals it.

options.text: A logo is more important than the brand
options.rationale: The logo is a part, not the whole.

options.text: A brand only exists once there is a logo
options.rationale: Perception exists independent of a logo.

items.explanation: Correct: the brand is the perception and relationship; the logo is one identifier.

items.stem: Which TWO are hallmarks of strong positioning? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It is relevant to a defined target audience
options.rationale: Correct: positioning must matter to a specific audience.

options.text: It tries to appeal to everyone
options.rationale: Appealing to everyone means standing for nothing.

items.explanation: Correct: strong positioning is both distinctive and relevant to a defined audience.

items.stem: A company wants its guidelines to actually produce consistent output. The guidelines should be treated as:

options.text: Rules a team applies consistently, with clear examples
options.rationale: Correct: guidelines only work when applied as rules with examples.
Guidelines need to be maintained and used.

items.explanation: Correct: guidelines must be applied as rules, with examples, to drive consistency.
